name: Swiss Poster
summary: International Typographic Style in motion: a visible modular grid on a warm grey page, white poster sheets built from black bars, one neo-grotesque, giant numerals beside tiny technical notes, one signal colour for the one protagonist, every move snapping onto a beat.

palette.use: ink: all type and the black bars
lead-ins and notes in medium grey (proposed)
grid lines on the page; the light-grey second-voice bars
signal: the one protagonist element (the red circle, the knife line); never a second
secondary bars (there is no second colour)
grid lines while they are being drawn

type.case: lowercase or sentence case statements; notes in sentence case
type.emphasis: scale contrast (a giant numeral beside tiny notes) and weight (regular vs bold); never colour except the signal element

banned: gradients, glow, shadows, particles, grain, device renders
words that fly, spin or bounce; overshoot, springs, bounce
fades and dissolves: everything wipes, clip-reveals or cuts
a second signal colour; colour used for emphasis
a Bauhaus pastiche of primary shapes; concentric-circle or fan layouts copied from historic posters
Helvetica or Akzidenz files; naming a real institution
rotating and labelling at the same time
too many thin columns (it reads as a chart)
centred layouts: flush left, ragged right

sources.what: Lemo-Opuscar style No. 16 "Swiss" (Swiss Motion Graphics): STYLE.md, DEMO.md, style.json
